title: Sher Singh and the ministers
hookLine: a new Maharaja, a court full of rivals, and a gun held out as a gift

lines: A COURTIER WITH A NEW GUN.
SHER SINGH, SON OF RANJIT SINGH.
cards: A courtier walks across a garden toward the Maharaja, carrying a new gun. He's come, the story goes, to show it off: a fine piece, worth a look. The Maharaja reaches for it.
In the histories of Lahore, that moment is where the court's long quarrel stops being whispers and becomes blood. The man on the throne is Sher Singh, a son of Ranjit Singh.
The man with the gun belongs to a family he had welcomed back to court.

teach.b: After the two heirs you met yesterday, Sher Singh came to power through a hard struggle with rivals inside the royal family.
He was brave and easygoing, the histories say, fond of hunting and company, and less fond of the daily work of holding a court together. Around him stood the men who really ran things.
Dhian Singh, the Dogra chief minister, you met at the court of many faiths. Against him stood the Sandhawalia sardars, kin of the royal house, with their own claims and grudges.
Each side watched the other. The Sandhawalias had fallen out with the court and been brought back into favor.
Then, as Cunningham and other histories tell it, Ajit Singh Sandhawalia came to Sher Singh with a gun to show him, and shot him with it. The Maharaja's young son Partap Singh was killed the same day.
Before the day was over, the Sandhawalias killed Dhian Singh too, the minister some accounts say had been in on the plot with them.
Then Dhian Singh's son, Hira Singh, turned the army against them, and they were killed in turn.

teach.h: ONE PLOT, A CIRCLE OF DEAD MEN.
teach.b: One plot, and a whole circle of men were dead.
In the first pauri, or stanza, of the Japji, Guru Nanak asks how a person can become truthful, and how the wall of falsehood can be torn down. His answer is to walk in the Lord's will.
Intrigue is falsehood made into a plan. It promises a safe path to power, and at Lahore it ended in a garden, a gun, and a line of graves.

how: Sikh histories remember the killing of Maharaja Sher Singh as part of the court intrigues that weakened the kingdom after Ranjit Singh, and Sikhs often point to the Gurus' warnings against falsehood when they tell it.

games.q: you're Sher Singh. a family that once quarreled with the court has come back into favor. one of them crosses the garden with a new gun to show you. what happens, as the histories tell it?
o: you reach for the gun, and he shoots you with it.
your guards take the gun first.
games.why: Ajit Singh Sandhawalia shot the Maharaja with the gun he'd brought to show him; the killing spread to his son and his chief minister.

practice: Bring to mind one place where quiet sides are forming, a group chat, an office, a family argument, and notice whether you've been pulled in, even a little.
Then picture yourself taking one step back, not cold and not superior, just out, and breathe there a while. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out.

wordCard.voice: Sher Singh, a son of Ranjit Singh, caught in a court split between rival families, and killed along with his son and his chief minister in a plot.
